Lessons.Title: Solutions to Systems of Linear Inequalities in Two Variables
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning objective: find pairs satisfying multiple two-variable constraints simultaneously and show graphically where half-planes overlap. Original Edulytiks material aligned with Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition U02:L24, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/2/24/preparation.html (CC BY 4.0). The source's quilting project combines a minimum total fabric amount and maximum cost, making a system rather than one inequality.

Independent quilt design: light fabric costs $9/yard and dark fabric $13/yard. At least 9.5 yards total are required while spending at most $110. Let l,d≥0 represent yards. The system is l+d≥9.5, 9l+13d≤110, l≥0, d≥0. Both equality lines are included; the solution region is their first-quadrant overlap.

Check (l,d)=(7,2.5): total 9.5 yards and cost $63+$32.50=$95.50, feasible. Pair (2,8): total 10 yards but price $18+$104=$122, outside budget. Lines intersect where d=6.125, l=3.375, meeting exactly 9.5 yards and $110. Use labels, units and included boundaries when graphing.

Student task: graph each original half-plane and the overlapping solution region, distinguish points meeting only one condition from points meeting both, then defend a candidate fabric allocation. Teacher-scored rubric 0–2 each for equations and domains, correctly shaded overlap, exact point tests, and justified interpretation including boundary inclusion.

KeyConcepts.Title: System of inequalities
KeyConcepts.Definition: Several inequalities restrict the same variables at once.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Every condition must hold for a valid pair.

KeyConcepts.Title: Region overlap
KeyConcepts.Definition: The system's graph is the intersection of all individual shaded regions.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Graph and test each half-plane separately.
KeyConcepts.Example: At least 9.5 yards and up to $110 form an overlapping wedge in the first quadrant.

KeyConcepts.Title: Boundary intersection
KeyConcepts.Definition: A point where related equality lines cross may mark a corner of the feasible set.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Solve both equalities then test domains.

WorkedExamples.Title: Check a feasible quilt purchase
WorkedExamples.Question: Is (7 light,2.5 dark) feasible?
WorkedExamples.Method: Interpret the stated inequality system, use valid domains and independently verify each numerical case.
WorkedExamples.Check: Both material and budget bounds verified.

WorkedExamples.Title: Reject a point satisfying only one condition
WorkedExamples.Question: Is (2 light,8 dark) feasible?
WorkedExamples.Method: Interpret the stated inequality system, use valid domains and independently verify each numerical case.
Steps: The pair is outside the overlapping feasible set.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find equality corner
WorkedExamples.Question: Solve l+d=9.5 and 9l+13d=110.
WorkedExamples.Method: Interpret the stated inequality system, use valid domains and independently verify each numerical case.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Shading the union rather than intersection
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A pair must satisfy BOTH constraints.
Negative yards do not describe a purchase.

SummaryPoints: Multiple conditions create an intersection of half-planes.
Fabric total and cost constraints must both be checked.
The equality lines meet at (3.375,6.125) yards.
Teacher reviews accurate overlapping region and contextual reasoning.
